content.body: Imagine you're searching for a specific song in a playlist that was accidentally shuffled, but you know the original order. How would you find it efficiently? We'll learn to search in a rotated sorted array using binary search principles.
content.title: Let's begin

content.body:
• Apply binary search to rotated sorted arrays.
• Implement the algorithm to find a target value.
• Explain why we check which half is sorted and how it helps eliminate search space.
content.title: What you'll learn

content.body: You have a rotated sorted array: [4,5,6,7,0,1,2]. The target is 0. Without writing code, think: How would you find 0? What's your first instinct? (We'll explore this together.)
content.title: Try it

content.body: You likely started scanning from the beginning or tried to guess where the rotation point is. That's natural! But scanning linearly doesn't scale well for large arrays.
content.title: What you did

content.body: When the array has millions of elements, checking each one is too slow. We need a method that cuts the search space dramatically at each step.
content.title: Why it gets hard

content.body: Binary search works by repeatedly cutting the range in half. For rotated arrays, we must first determine which half is properly sorted, because only one half can contain the answer. This lets us eliminate the other half.
content.title: Key idea
content.visualMetaphor: Repeatedly cut the range in half; only one half can contain the answer.

content.body: We'll use binary search with a twist: at each step, check if the left or right half is sorted. If the target lies within the sorted half, search there; otherwise, search the other half. This way, we always eliminate half the possibilities.
content.title: The approach

content.body:
1. Set left and right pointers.
2. While left <= right, find the midpoint.
3. Check if the left half (left to mid) is sorted.
4. If sorted and target is in that range, search left; else search right.
5. If right half (mid to right) is sorted and target is in that range, search right; else search left.
6. Repeat until found or pointers cross.

content.body: You've successfully implemented search in a rotated sorted array! Remember: binary search works by cutting the range in half, but in rotated arrays, we must first identify which half is sorted to know where the target could be. Always check: is the left half sorted? If yes, is the target within it? This lets us eliminate half the possibilities each step.
